sem_data.subject: BCA-5003 Computer Network
sem_data.topic: Unit IV — Transport Layer: TCP Congestion Control Mechanisms (Slow Start, AIMD, Fast Retransmit & Reno)
detailed_notes: Network congestion occurs when the aggregate traffic injected into a network exceeds the capacity of intermediate routers and links, causing buffer overflow, queuing delays, and packet drops (Congestion Collapse). TCP incorporates end-to-end congestion control to dynamically modulate transmission rates without explicit router feedback.

Key State Variables:
• Congestion Window (`cwnd`): The maximum number of bytes the sender is permitted to transmit before receiving an ACK, dynamically calculated by the sender.
• Advertised Window (`rwnd`): The buffer capacity advertised by the receiver in the TCP header for flow control.
• Effective Sending Window = `min(cwnd, rwnd)`.
• Slow Start Threshold (`ssthresh`): The window size threshold determining the transition between Slow Start and Congestion Avoidance.

The 4 Core Phases of TCP Congestion Control:
1. Slow Start Phase:
• Initially `cwnd = 1 MSS` (Maximum Segment Size). `ssthresh` is typically set to 64KB.
• For EVERY ACK received, `cwnd` increases by 1 MSS: `cwnd = cwnd + 1 MSS`.
• This causes `cwnd` to DOUBLE every Round Trip Time (RTT): 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8 -> 16 MSS (Exponential Growth!).
• Continues until `cwnd >= ssthresh` or a packet drop occurs.

2. Congestion Avoidance Phase (Additive Increase):
• Once `cwnd >= ssthresh`, exponential growth stops to prevent abrupt network saturation.
• For every RTT, `cwnd` increases by strictly 1 MSS (Additive Increase): `cwnd = cwnd + (1 / cwnd)` per ACK.
• Graphically represents a linear staircase ascent.

3. Multiplicative Decrease (Handling Packet Loss):
• Case A (Timeout): Severe congestion indicator. `ssthresh = cwnd / 2`, `cwnd` is collapsed to 1 MSS, and Slow Start restarts.
• Case B (3 Duplicate ACKs): Mild packet loss. Router dropped 1 segment, but subsequent segments arrived at receiver.
4. Fast Retransmit & Fast Recovery (TCP Reno):
• Fast Retransmit: Sender retransmits the missing segment immediately upon receiving the 3rd duplicate ACK WITHOUT waiting for retransmission timer expiration!
• Fast Recovery (TCP Reno): Instead of dropping `cwnd` to 1 MSS (as in TCP Tahoe), Reno sets `ssthresh = cwnd / 2` and `cwnd = ssthresh + 3 MSS`, continuing Congestion Avoidance without restarting Slow Start.

rows: Starts at 1 MSS, ends when cwnd >= ssthresh
Triggered by receipt of 3 Duplicate ACKs

sem_data.memorize: AIMD: Additive Increase (+1 MSS/RTT), Multiplicative Decrease (halve ssthresh on loss). Tahoe resets cwnd to 1; Reno halves cwnd to ssthresh on 3 dup ACKs.
sem_data.understand: Why does Slow Start double exponentially? To rapidly discover the available network link capacity without wasting dozens of RTTs crawling upwards linearly from 1 MSS.
sem_data.common_mistakes: 1. Assuming Slow Start increases by 1 segment per RTT (it doubles every RTT!). 2. Confusing flow control (protects receiver buffer via rwnd) with congestion control (protects network routers via cwnd).
sem_data.pyq_question: Explain TCP Congestion Control in detail. Describe Slow Start, Congestion Avoidance, Fast Retransmit, and Fast Recovery with a neat cwnd graph. Differentiate between TCP Tahoe and TCP Reno. (15 Marks)
sem_data.pyq_rubric: Concept of Congestion & cwnd vs rwnd (3 marks) + 4 Phases explained with formulas (6 marks) + CWND graph (3 marks) + Tahoe vs Reno comparison (3 marks) = 15 Marks.
model_answer_paragraphs: Flow control is an end-to-end mechanism between sender and receiver preventing receiver buffer overflow (regulated via `rwnd`). Congestion control is a global network mechanism preventing intermediate router buffer exhaustion and link saturation (regulated via `cwnd`). Effective transmission window = min(cwnd, rwnd).
2. Detailed Breakdown of TCP Congestion Control Mechanisms:

• Slow Start: Starts with cwnd = 1 MSS. Each received ACK increments cwnd by 1 MSS, doubling cwnd every RTT (1, 2, 4, 8...). Once cwnd reaches `ssthresh`, mode switches to Congestion Avoidance.
• Congestion Avoidance: Employs Additive Increase: cwnd increases by 1 MSS per RTT regardless of the number of ACKs received. Represents linear probe of bandwidth.
• Fast Retransmit: When a single segment is lost, receiver sends duplicate ACKs for subsequent out-of-order packets. Upon receiving 3 Duplicate ACKs, sender retransmits the missing segment immediately without waiting for timeout.
• Fast Recovery: Avoids dropping to cwnd = 1 MSS. Halves ssthresh and sets cwnd = ssthresh, resuming linear congestion avoidance.

In TCP Tahoe, ANY packet loss (timeout or 3 duplicate ACKs) forces cwnd back down to 1 MSS, re-entering slow start. In TCP Reno, 3 duplicate ACKs trigger Fast Recovery: cwnd is halved to `ssthresh` and continues linear growth, avoiding severe throughput collapse.

apt_data.topic: Data Interpretation (DI) — Tables, Bar Charts & Missing Data
tutorial: Data Interpretation (DI) tests rapid quantitative extraction and mental percentage calculation from complex datasets.

Core Mathematical Operations in DI:
1. Percentage Growth: % Increase/Decrease = [(Final Value - Initial Value) / Initial Value] * 100.
2. Ratio Comparison: To compare A/B vs C/D, cross-multiply A*D vs B*C.
3. Average: Sum of items / Total item count.
4. Approximations: Round numbers to 2 significant digits (e.g., 4,821 / 15,920 ≈ 48 / 160 = 30%).
apt_data.formulas: Growth % = (Change / Base) * 100. Ratio cross-multiplication: A/B > C/D if A*D > B*C.
apt_data.shortcut: Splitting the Base for Percentages: To find 17% of 420: 10% = 42, 5% = 21, 1% = 4.2. Total = 42 + 21 + (2 * 4.2) = 71.4.
apt_data.recognition: Look for multi-column tables showing year-over-year production, sales, or expenditures in TCS NQT, Wipro, and Cognizant.
apt_data.tier1_problem: A table shows sales (in lakhs) of 3 products (A, B, C) over 2 years: Year 1: A=40, B=60, C=80. Year 2: A=50, B=75, C=100. Find the overall percentage increase in total sales.
apt_data.tier1_solution:
Total Sales Year 1 = 40 + 60 + 80 = 180 lakhs.
Total Sales Year 2 = 50 + 75 + 100 = 225 lakhs.
Absolute Increase = 225 - 180 = 45 lakhs.
Percentage Increase = (45 / 180) * 100 = (1 / 4) * 100 = 25%. Answer: 25%.
apt_data.tier2_problem: A company has 5 departments with employees: IT: 120, HR: 40, Sales: 80, Finance: 60, Ops: 100. What percentage of the total workforce is in Sales?
apt_data.tier2_solution:
Total Workforce = 120 + 40 + 80 + 60 + 100 = 400.
Sales employees = 80.
Percentage = (80 / 400) * 100 = 20%. Answer: 20%.
apt_data.tier3_problem:
[TCS NQT DI Pattern] Table shows Revenue and Expenditure (in Crores) of a firm across 4 years:
2021: Rev=200, Exp=160
2022: Rev=250, Exp=190
2023: Rev=300, Exp=210
2024: Rev=360, Exp=240
In which year was the Profit Percentage [(Rev - Exp) / Exp * 100] the highest?
apt_data.tier4_problem: A table has missing data for student marks. Total students = 200. Passed in Math = 140. Passed in Science = 120. If 30 students failed both subjects, how many students passed in BOTH subjects?
apt_data.tier4_solution:
Total Students = 200.
Students failing both = 30 ==> Students passing at least one subject = 200 - 30 = 170.
Using Set Theory: n(M union S) = n(M) + n(S) - n(M intersection S).
170 = 140 + 120 - n(Both)
170 = 260 - n(Both)
n(Both) = 260 - 170 = 90 students. Answer: 90 students.

dsa_problems.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence (LeetCode 300 - Medium)
dsa_problems.importance: Top-tier Placement Dynamic Programming Problem (Google, Amazon, TCS Digital)
dsa_problems.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
dsa_problems.solution_approach:
Approach 1: Classic DP in O(N^2):
Let dp[i] represent the length of the LIS ending at index i.
For every j < i: if nums[j] < nums[i], dp[i] = max(dp[i], dp[j] + 1).

Approach 2: Patience Sorting with Binary Search in O(N log N):
Maintain an array `tails` where tails[k] stores the smallest tail of all increasing subsequences of length k+1.
For each x in nums, use binary search (`bisect_left`) to find its insertion position in `tails`. If x is greater than all elements, append it; otherwise replace the existing element.
line_by_line: Dynamic array maintaining the smallest active tail for every subsequence length.
Binary search in O(log N) to find insertion or replacement index.
Extends the maximum subsequence length found so far.
Greedily lowers the tail value of an existing length, increasing chances for future expansions.
dsa_problems.time_complexity: O(N log N) using binary search (or O(N^2) using basic DP).
dsa_problems.edge_cases: Strictly decreasing array [7, 7, 7] (returns 1); sorted array [1, 2, 3] (returns len).

cs_core.subject: Operating Systems
cs_core.topic: Process Synchronization Primitives: Semaphores, Mutexes & Condition Variables
detailed_notes:
Critical Section Problem:
A section of code accessing shared resources that must not be concurrently accessed by more than one process. Must satisfy 3 criteria: 1. Mutual Exclusion, 2. Progress, 3. Bounded Waiting.

Synchronization Primitives Compared:
• Mutex (Mutual Exclusion Lock): A locking mechanism with ownership. Only the thread that locked the mutex is permitted to unlock it. Binary state (locked/unlocked).
• Semaphore (Dijkstra): A signaling integer counter variable accessed only via atomic operations `wait()` (P) and `signal()` (V).
  - Counting Semaphore: Counter value N represents available units of a shared resource.
  - Binary Semaphore: Value restricted to 0 or 1. Unlike a mutex, a semaphore has NO ownership: Thread A can wait() and Thread B can signal() to release it!
• Spinlock: Thread busy-waits in a loop checking lock state. Useful on multi-core systems when lock duration is shorter than OS context-switch overhead.

Priority Inversion Problem:
Occurs when a low-priority thread holds a shared lock needed by a high-priority thread, and a medium-priority thread preempts the low-priority thread, starving the high-priority thread! Solved by Priority Inheritance Protocol (low-priority thread temporarily inherits high priority while holding lock).

interview_qa.q: What is the technical difference between a Mutex and a Binary Semaphore?
interview_qa.a: The fundamental difference is 'ownership' and purpose. A Mutex is a locking mechanism with ownership: the exact same thread that acquired the mutex MUST release it. A Binary Semaphore is a signaling mechanism without ownership: one thread can wait for an event, and a completely different thread or interrupt service routine can signal the semaphore to unblock it.

interview_qa.q: What is Priority Inversion and how does Priority Inheritance solve it?
interview_qa.a: Priority inversion happens when a low-priority process holds a lock required by a high-priority process, but is preempted by an unrelated medium-priority process, indefinitely delaying the high-priority process. Priority Inheritance solves this by temporarily elevating the priority of the low-priority lock-holder to match the waiting high-priority process until the lock is released.

project_defense.feature_focus: System Design: Scaling BulkBeat TV to 50k Concurrent Users
project_defense.architecture_deep_dive:
Scaling BulkBeat TV from a single VPS to 50,000 concurrent streaming users:

1. Decoupled Architecture:
Separate media stream ingestion from user notification distribution. The ingestion pipeline runs as an isolated worker service, writing stream events to an Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ message broker.

2. Distributed Caching & Database Tier:
• Migrate embedded SQLite to a PostgreSQL cluster with 1 Primary (Writes) and 3 Read Replicas.
• Place a Redis cluster in front of PostgreSQL to cache active subscription tokens and channel metadata with a 60-second TTL, reducing database load by 95%.

3. Horizontal API Gateway Scaling:
Deploy FastAPI stateless containers behind Nginx / AWS ALB using round-robin load balancing. WebSocket connections are terminated at the load balancer with Redis Pub/Sub syncing broadcast messages across server instances.

interview_qa.q: How would you handle sudden traffic spikes during breaking news events on BulkBeat TV?
interview_qa.a: I would implement aggressive edge caching via a CDN (Cloudflare) for static assets and public stream playlists. For dynamic user notifications, I would decouple alert publishing from delivery using an asynchronous Redis Pub/Sub message broker, buffering outgoing traffic and protecting backend workers from connection spikes.

interview_qa.q: Why is Redis Pub/Sub suitable for multi-instance WebSocket synchronization?
interview_qa.a: When multiple FastAPI server instances run behind a load balancer, client WebSockets are scattered across different physical machines. Redis Pub/Sub acts as a lightweight central event bus: when an alert occurs, the producer publishes to a Redis channel, and all server instances receive the event simultaneously and push it down their local active WebSocket connections.

questions.q: What is the update rule for TCP Slow Start for each received ACK?
questions.a: cwnd = cwnd + 1 MSS. The congestion window doubles every round trip time.

questions.q: How does TCP Reno handle packet loss signaled by 3 Duplicate ACKs?
questions.a: It triggers Fast Retransmit and Fast Recovery: ssthresh is set to cwnd / 2, and cwnd is set to ssthresh, continuing linear congestion avoidance without restarting slow start.

questions.q: If revenue increases from 200 Cr to 260 Cr, what is the percentage increase?
What is the time complexity of the optimized Patience Sorting solution for LIS?
questions.a: O(N log N) using binary search (bisect_left) on the tails array.

questions.q: What are the 3 criteria that any valid solution to the Critical Section problem must satisfy?
Can a Binary Semaphore be unlocked by a thread other than the one that locked it?
questions.a: Yes. Semaphores are signaling mechanisms and have no ownership, unlike Mutexes.

questions.q: What is the difference between TCP Tahoe and TCP Reno on 3 Duplicate ACKs?
questions.a: Tahoe drops cwnd back to 1 MSS and restarts Slow Start. Reno halves cwnd to ssthresh and enters Fast Recovery.

questions.q: How does Priority Inheritance resolve Priority Inversion in OS synchronization?
questions.a: The low-priority thread holding the lock temporarily inherits the higher priority of the waiting thread until it releases the shared lock.
